headline_marked: UK Home Office [[launches £75M PoliceAI]] centre for AI in policing
headline: UK Home Office launches £75M PoliceAI centre for AI in policing
summary: The new centre will identify, test, and scale AI tools for police forces across England and Wales, aiming to free up millions of police hours annually.
details: The UK Home Office has officially launched PoliceAI, a new national centre dedicated to expanding the use of artificial intelligence in policing for England and Wales. This initiative is backed by a £75 million investment over the next three years, as part of a broader £140 million AI investment by 2028-29.

PoliceAI will collaborate with all police forces to find, test, and implement AI solutions that deliver tangible results. In its first year, the centre will focus on areas where AI can provide immediate benefits, such as piloting AI tools to help officers triage, disclose, and summarize digital evidence, a notoriously time-consuming task.

The goal is to significantly reduce the time officers spend on administrative tasks. The Home Office estimates that AI redaction tools alone could free up one million staff hours annually if adopted by all forces. Large-scale pilots for evidence analysis are expected to be scaled up to all forces by 2027.

The impact of AI in policing is already being demonstrated. A trial using AI to review 800 hours of footage in a kidnapping case was completed in just three hours, leading to an early guilty plea. Another instance saw AI translate half a million e-books of data instantly, resulting in the arrest of an organized crime gang.

Policing minister Sarah Jones stated that PoliceAI will transform policing by improving data access, generating new leads, and freeing up the equivalent of 3,000 officers. She emphasized the commitment to responsible AI deployment with public consent.

The centre will also focus on tackling tool theft and retail crime, with a £1 million investment to integrate police data with property marking schemes and use AI to identify stolen goods and track their resale online. This aims to return more property to victims and increase frontline policing.

PoliceAI will maintain a public registry of AI tools used in policing, developed in partnership with Sheffield Hallam University's CENTRIC research centre. An initial version of this registry is anticipated by autumn this year. AI models will undergo independent testing for accuracy and bias.

topic: show hn make pdfs look scanned cli or browser wasm
headline_marked: [[Make PDFs look scanned]] with CLI or browser WASM tool
headline: Make PDFs look scanned with CLI or browser WASM tool
summary: This new tool degrades PDFs to mimic physical scans, complete with realistic imperfections, and runs both locally and in the browser.
details: A new command-line interface (CLI) tool has been released that can transform digital PDFs into documents that appear to have been physically scanned. It simulates common scanner imperfections such as skew, grayscale conversion, paper tone variations, grain, defocus, edge shadows, and JPEG compression artifacts.

The tool offers deterministic output by default, meaning the same input file will always produce the same scanned appearance. This is achieved by deriving a seed from the input PDF's content, though users can specify a seed for reproducible variations.

Beyond the CLI, the effect pipeline is also available in the browser via WebAssembly (WASM). This version uses PDF.js for rasterization and then applies the same Go effects, offering a visually equivalent experience without byte-for-byte identical output due to differences in rasterization engines.
The browser build is a single, self-contained HTML file that includes the WASM module, Go runtime glue, and PDF.js, allowing it to run offline directly in a browser without needing a server.

The project's licensing is AGPL-3.0 due to its use of MuPDF via go-fitz in the CLI version. Distributing the CLI binary requires sharing its source code. The browser build, however, uses Apache-2.0 licensed PDF.js and does not include MuPDF.
caption:
